PRECAUTIONS
1. The crucible should be heated to a constant weight.
2. All the glasswares should be handled with care.
3. There should be a small gap between the crucible and its lid during
heating so as to let the water vapours escape off.

THEORY

When copper sulphate solution is treated with bench sodium hydroxide then a bluish white precipitate of cupric hydroxide is obtained. The precipitate on heating strongly decomposes to give black oxide of copper (cupric oxide). + NaS04 cuS04 + 2NaOH bluish white ppt Cuo + H20 black residue The black oxide can be reduced to red oxide of copper (cuprous oxide) in presence of a reducing agent like glucose. When cupric oxide is heated with glucose solution, residue of red oxide is obtained. 2CuO (s) + C6H1206 (aq) ------.-2---—cu20 (s) + C5H1105. COOH (aq) red residue gluconic acid The purity of the black oxide can be checked by treating the residue Washed water with few drops of BaC12 solution. Presence of sulphate ion in the residue is indicated by formation of a white ppt.

PROCEDURE
Preparation of black oxide of copper A. Take a test tubeful of strong solution of copper sulphate in a beaker.
Add bench sodium hydroxide so as to obtain a bluish white precipitate.
Allow the solution to stand for some time in order to settle down the precipitate. To the supernatant liquid, add a drop of bench NaOH.
If a fresh ppt appears, add few more drops of bench NaOH. Again' check for the completeness of precipitation as in No. (3).
If no fresh ppt appears, then heat the solution strongly.
Black residue will be formed. When no more black residue is formed' filter the solution.
Wash the residue 2-3 times with distilled water.
Take few drops of residue-washed water coming out from the stem of the funnel in a test tube. To this, add few drops of barium chloride solution.
Miscellaneous If a white precipitate appears, this means the black oxide0 is contaminated with SOC - ions (Na2S04 solution). Wash the ppt agarn.
When no more ppt is produced by the residue-washed water with BaC12 solution, then leave the black residue to dry in air.
Preparation of red oxide of copper B. To the black oxide of copper as prepared above, add a test tubeful of concentrated solution of glucose.
Heat the solution. The black oxide converts into the red oxide. If the red oxide is not formed so easily, add more glucose solution.
Filter the solution. Leave the red residue to dry in air.
Study of properties of the oxides C. Add concentrated sulphuric acid to a pinch of the black oxide in a test tube. A blue colouration will be seen.
Heat a pinch of the red oxide strongly in air in a test tube. It gets converted into the black oxide.
Treat a pinch of the red oxide with conc. HCl. Being a basic oxide, it reacts with conc. HCl giving a white precipitate of cuprous chloride.
